_about: Jupiter (USAF Band wind-ensemble recording, charted from the orchestral MusicXML). Places where the band arrangement differs from the orchestral score, confirmed by ear. Same entry types as the other songs' corrections files (score seconds).

merge.why: 1:25 (score 90.53-91.94): the orchestral oboe re-strikes 76 76 and drops to 64, but the band's woodwinds strike the 76 at 90.24, strike it once more and hold through the bar. The recording can't settle it alone (the bass walk attacks on every beat). Confirmed by ear Nov 15: D76, then D76 held.

4:52 (score 334.59): the band's final chord of the tune rings until the woodwind entries; the orchestral violins re-strike 89 in quarters (the tag the band doesn't play). One held note (user, by ear, Nov 16).
6:17 (score 456.18-457.1): the woodwinds re-strike 67 in quarters under the flutes' held note; you hear one held note with the flutes (user, by ear, Nov 16).

lead_part.why: 1:31-1:33 (score 97.0-99.0): between phrases the orchestral first violins walk down 76 72 69 67 under the flutes' running figure. In the band it's a faint clarinet line, background between the main phrases, so nothing plays until the oboe's 72 pickup starts the next phrase. Confirmed by ear Nov 15.

3:03.6 (score 198.81): the band's short chord ending the fast section; the rules pick the timpani's 43 under it, but the ear hears the top (clarinets / first violins, 79). A general 'timpani isn't the line' rule would change Arabesque's approved timpani hits at 2:40, so it's a correction (Nov 16).
5:28 (score 405.8-408.4): the band swells on one big held chord; the clarinets' 83 76 71 eighth-note cycle under it isn't what you hear (user, by ear, Nov 16). The chord's top, held.
5:45 (score 425.89): in the silence between the trumpets' calls the bassoons (with low strings) walk up 50 55 60 62 into the oboes (user, by ear, Nov 16).
6:12-6:13 (score 452.43-453.8): the woodwinds' scale flourish 50 ... 86 is what you hear; the horns' and violas' 50s under it read as stray taps (user, by ear, Nov 16).
6:35 (score 475.39-477.27): the horns' moving 55 60 65 | 57 62 67 is the melody; the woodwinds just hold 79 / 74 above it (user, by ear, Nov 16).
6:50-6:57 (score 490.89-498.8): the horns' line 67 69 70 69 67 | 67 69 62 64 ... is the main line; the woodwinds' arpeggio flourishes over it can't be heard in the band (user, by ear, Nov 16).
7:00 (score 499.23): the trumpets' call 67 72 77 69 74 79 (answered by the woodwinds at 501.23) is the interesting part, over the low unison 60 55 57 58 line (user, by ear, Nov 16).

audio_moves.why: 1:21.7 (score 87.07-87.65): the woodwinds' 85 81 78 after the held 78 came out a full eighth early -- the alignment latched onto a weak attack. The recording's strong attacks (with the band's 52 on the downbeat) are at 81.98 / 82.22 / 82.46 (user, by ear, Nov 16).

time_map.why: 4:55-5:04 (score 338-366.5): the band takes the woodwinds' one-two-three entries about three times faster than the score's tempo marking, and the warp crumpled them. One steady line through the entries' top notes in the recording: 343.71->296.81, 346.71->297.73, 349.71->298.62, 356.46->300.71, 359.46->301.64, 361.71->302.34, 364.71->303.24 (0.306s per written second), so every entry is evenly spaced. Nov 16.
5:04-5:10: the rest of the passage, meeting the alignment again at 386.46 (309.75).

5:56-6:00 (score 436-440): the trumpets' 69 72 74 triplets keep a steady pace in the band (attacks every ~0.22s, 356.68 ... 360.40); the score's slight ritardando and the warp made the chart slow down where nobody does (user, by ear, Nov 16).

6:12.7-6:14 (score 452.43-453.83): the woodwinds' scale flourish 50 ... 86 came out with its first dozen notes stacked on one instant; laid out evenly from its first note to the piccolo/oboe entry that follows it (Nov 16).

7:41-7:44 (score 546.27-549.09): the brass/timpani fanfare on C. Its attacks in the recording run 461.05 ... 463.71 (last stroke), and the trumpets' half-note build starts at 463.95; the warp let the last stroke drift to 464.2, crowding the first half note (user, Nov 17: 'weird pattern').

7:44-7:50 (score 549.09-553.71): the trumpets' half notes 72 77 82 | 74 79 into the final chord. The recording's attacks (and pitches) are 463.95 (72), 464.7 (77), 465.43 (82), 466.54 (74), 466.91 (79), final chord 468.43 -- the written rhythm at a steady pace. The earlier map started them half a second late, which squeezed them into an uneven pattern (user, Nov 17: 'the end should be half notes'). The final chord is a hit (user, Nov 17).

7:27-7:28.6 (score 528.94-530.94): the low line's last D J D (44 46 44) and the 42 under the trumpets' entry. The recording's low notes come in at 446.97 (32/44), 447.47 (34/46), 448.07 (32/44), 448.6 (30/42); the warp had them about 0.15s late (user, Nov 17: 'the last DJD in the low melody is late by a little bit').
7:28.07-7:28.6 (score 529.94-530.94): the low line's held 44 (448.07) into the bass's 42 under the trumpets' entry (448.6); see the entry before.

7:28.6-7:29.7 (score 530.94-531.94): the trumpets' pickups 63 66 into their held 68. The held note lands with the bass's 39 at 449.7 (user, by ear, Nov 17: 'around 7:29.71'); the pickups start with the bass's 42 at 448.6.

7:29.7-7:37 (score 531.94-539.94): the trumpets' broad melody from the held 68 (449.7, user) to the 74 at 457.0, a steady 0.91s per written second (matches a pitch fit of the trumpet line against the recording).

rests.why: 4:52-4:55 (score 334.6-338.2): after the band's last chord of the tune (334.59, kept as a held chord) the orchestral score has a quarter-note tag (flutes 89 87, clarinets 75 77 70 ..., then the clarinets' held 77); in the band recording only that chord dies away until the woodwind entries (user, by ear, Nov 16).
5:30 (score 408.15): the violins' re-strike of the chord top at the end of the swell -- part of the swell, not a new note (Nov 16).

chord_passages.why: 4:52.15: the band's final chord of the tune (every part strikes it), held as a chord (user, by ear, Nov 16).

missing_parts.why: 5:32 (score 411.1): the trumpets' walk down 72 71 69 stops, but the second violins (with them) finish it on 67 -- the four-note walk down you hear (user, by ear, Nov 16).

thin.why: 6:12 (score 452.43-453.8): the woodwinds' 22-note scale 50 ... 86 (about 16 notes a second) is too dense to tap; every other note keeps the rising sweep (user's choice, Nov 16).

song_end_why: The band's last chord (7:48.4) dies away by about 7:50; the file runs on in silence to 8:00 (user, Nov 17).
